defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: Absolute NETRC paths get ~/ prefix via expanduser, resolving to /home/user//etc/netrc
Empty NETRC string treats home directory as netrc file
Relative NETRC paths incorrectly prefixed with ~/
Implementation inverts NETRC convention by treating it as filename relative to HOME
No test for absolute NETRC path
Docstring omits NETRC env var documentation
votes.evidence_quote: When the user sets `NETRC=/etc/netrc`, the code constructs `os.path.expanduser("~//etc/netrc")`, which resolves to `/home/user//etc/netrc` — not `/etc/netrc`.
votes.justification: Finding 1 reports the same defect at the expanduser call. The ~/ prefix is applied to an absolute NETRC path, so the file outside home is never found. Findings 3 and 4 describe the same root cause from other angles: explicit paths get the ~/ template, which inverts the convention that NETRC holds a full path.
